title.en: Können, müssen, dürfen and möchten: modal verbs + infinitive

summary.en: Put can, must, or may in the verb slot and send the action verb in its -en form to the end.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 2 and 3.

Early in episode one, Martin sighs *Ich muss* read the ledger—sending *lesen* to the end of his clause. In the breakfast kitchen he asks *Können wir* salted butter with jam *servieren*?, and upstairs Lukas politely asks *Darf ich* the attic room first *anschauen*?

German modal verbs—*können* (can), *müssen* (must / have to), *dürfen* (may / be allowed to), *wollen* (want to), *sollen* (should), plus polite *möchten* (would like, as in *Möchten Sie*?)—build a clean two-part frame. The modal conjugates for the speaker (notice no `-e` or `-t` ending on singular *Ich muss* or *Darf ich*), while the main action verb stands unchanged in its `-en` dictionary form at the very end.

When a separable verb like *anschauen* meets a modal like *dürfen*, prefix and verb stay glued together as one word at the end!

On replay, listen for the modal up front and the full `-en` verb—*lesen*, *servieren*, *anschauen*—closing each thought.
